sections.value:
Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES
PR: #277
Head: f9d2bc77871f3d7cee6418d6d18c86c26d5e40f4
Base: df01a3380f8958856f5636fc1f98f4acbe1f7b8e
Request: 01a1f68b-e561-7983-977c-baa89ebf7ee1

No high-confidence blocking security vulnerability was identified in the
changes under C33's user-account trust boundary. This is a security verdict,
not an assertion that all requested functional properties are satisfied.
No product files were modified.

Acceptance notes requiring the PM/correctness reviewer's disposition:

1. D2 has global overflow loss, not cross-seat isolation.
   crates/daemon/src/registration/refusals.rs:19-46 removes expired entries
   but never evicts unexpired ones. At 512 occupied pairs every unseen
   seat/code pair is suppressed until expiry, including another seat's
   first refusal. Existing pairs do not have their timestamps refreshed by
   suppressed retries. Thus "cannot suppress another seat's refusals" is
   not a property of this implementation. Same-user deliberate saturation
   is outside C33's hostile-principal model, but ordinary traffic above
   the cap also loses visibility. Registration results are unchanged;
   publication is awaited, so strict latency-independent nonblocking
   behavior is not established.

2. The deadline-ready banner is diagnostic, not daemon acceptance proof.
   .copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:730-765,1749-1760 treats its local
   claim wait timeout as recovery. An actual in-memory fetch probe received
   a 401, then never submitted the next inbox request; the local deadline
   still emitted connection-ready. No native send occurred. This is a
   demonstrated false-ready diagnostic, not an authorization or ACK bypass.
   Received refusals/4xx, external aborts, connection failures and stalled
   response bodies do not themselves enter that branch. Returned messages
   and valid empty claims end the outage. Not clearing on registration
   or heartbeat is sound: the independent re-registration mutant made the
   existing bounded-backoff test report 7 banners instead of 1.

3. D1 history is daemon-incarnation-scoped, not durably alternating.
   crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:363-369,426-465,512-524,596-610,705-726
   initializes an empty set and applies the existing boot grace. Within
   an instance, insertion tells a lapse once and heartbeat removal tells
   a renewal only after an observed lapse. Both receiver and edge maps
   prune non-live/non-native/tombstoned seats. The set does not remember a
   pre-restart event; a still-lapsed seat can be observed again after the
   new boot grace. Failed publication consumes the edge without retry.
   Therefore durable no-double-tell across daemon restarts is not proven.

Security evidence:

- registration.rs:286-395 constructs the observation from a named
  descriptor or an exact name already retained by Attempts::names.
  Payload fields are seat plus closed enum-derived code and attempt
  labels. IMPORTANT: attempt is a string path label, not a numeric count.
  Raw refusal explanations, warning/credential text, tokens, environment
  and home paths are not copied into these new normal observations.
- registration/attempts.rs:102-129,177-191,245-267,298-306 normalizes
  arbitrary client attempt labels to other, bounds retained names to
  64 bytes, and does not retain unknown failed addresses as names.
  http/mod.rs:1128-1197 counts malformed early claims without telling them.
  core/src/model.rs:46-79 and registration.rs:1144-1153 enforce the
  bounded lowercase/digit/hyphen pij identifier grammar for new IDs.
  No new registry read is used to establish a telemetry name.
- delivery/mod.rs:480-506 emits seat and numeric/null renewed_at.
  Legacy stored IDs remain trusted; generic sink-error diagnostics still
  interpolate internal errors. This is not a blanket claim that every
  possible failure log contains only the normal observation fields.
- http/tests.rs:2790-2819 retains the exact alias call-history invariant;
  http/tests.rs:4983-5045 retains an empty registry call list for invalid
  process evidence. native_tests.rs:428-445 retains unchanged owner/queue
  assertions. tests/role_http.rs:793-852 retains escaping, absent probe
  seat, and unchanged-folder checks. The relaxed comparisons allow only
  registration.refused, not arbitrary event publication.
- pa_watchdog.rs:1446-1473 builds advisory FleetAnomaly text with
  shell_word quoting; core/src/directory.rs:32-41 safely quotes apostrophes.
  The new restart suggestion is never executed by this path.
- No new managed_plugins or model_http trigger was added. Existing
  session.error classification remains unchanged; do not broaden triggers
  based on this verdict.

Independently observed proof:

- just pr-freeze 277: PASS twice, exact head FINAL and checkout clean.
- Exact-head ci run 44652231462: successful; rust-test job 136009674366
  reports 2603 tests passed, 6 skipped. Its successful upload log identifies
  JUnit artifact 14592210106. That exact artifact was parsed independently:
  D1 lapse/renewal, D2 per-window/expiry and bounded-capacity tests,
  made-up-name refusal, unchanged transient owner/queue, restart-digest
  advice, and control-character folder tests all passed (7 named cases).
- just copilot-native-test: PASS, 363 passed, zero failed, three
  Linux-only skips on this macOS checkout.
- Existing exact-source Node banner tests: baseline 3/3 passed.
  In-memory source mutations removing deadline-ready and clearing on
  re-registration were both caught by those actual tests.
- D2 COMPILED SOURCE MUTATIONS: the complete exact-head refusals.rs module
  was compiled independently with rustc --test, using its existing Tokio
  library dependency and temporary outputs, all at niceness 19.
  Original tests: 2/2 PASS. Occupied-entry false-to-true mutation:
  caught, duplicate-refusal assertion failed (exit 101).
  Capacity >= to > mutation: caught, first-overflow assertion failed
  (exit 101). Temporary compiler outputs were removed automatically.
  This compiles the actual D2 module, not a translated model; it does not
  rebuild the entire daemon.
- D1 SOURCE-DERIVED MODEL MUTATIONS: baseline eight assertions passed;
  always-tell lapse, contains-instead-of-remove renewal, and stale-marker
  pruning mutants were caught. These are restricted Python interpretations
  of exact-source guards, NOT compiled Rust/Tokio/integration mutant proof.
  No full-daemon D1 Rust mutation run was performed. The exact-head D1
  integration baseline is established by CI, not by these model mutations.
- Previously run cached local Rust binaries were not proven bound to this
  head and are not used as exact-head compilation evidence here.

Gate and live-proof limits:

harness boot --json returned advisory ready:false because this read-only
review worktree has no node_modules. No dependencies were installed or
symlinked. Full harness checks was not rerun: the live omp-config sensor
can touch shared settings, and C25 keeps missing-dependency TS proof
CI-only. No claim is made that the full local gate passed.
No deployment, daemon bounce, live lapse experiment or before/after fleet
cost measurement was performed.

Static cost:

No new process launch, polling loop, timer or automatic action. Existing
reconciliation runs every 5 seconds plus receiver-deadline wakes. D1 adds
an in-memory edge-map prune (worst-case lapsed seats times live seats per
reconciliation) and edge-only log/event writes. D2 scans at most 512
in-memory pairs per service refusal, with one normal event/log per admitted
pair per ten minutes; global saturation suppresses new pairs as noted.
The dedupe window is a brake on noise: removing it only tells more.
The restart text is advice; no new destructive policy or action is added.

Harness feedback:

difficulties: A verdict-only specialist response omitted completed proof;
saved tool receipts had to be recovered before publication.
magicWand: Require structured command/result, file/line, mutation and
proof-limit receipts from no-findings review reports. Existing role memory
already records this recurring gap; no new product scope is proposed here.
